subject: frostAxe
pitch:
Category: Fantasy weapon.
Subject: frost-forged battle axe.
Style: League of Legends.
reasoning:
Looking at the renders, I notice the axe blade on one side reads fine from the front but the haft looks too thin and spear-like from the side angle. The gold root plate also appears muddy brown rather than looking like proper bronze.

The haft proportions seem off relative to the overall axe size, and the rear fluke is too dark with low contrast compared to the ice-edged main blade. I want to fix this by applying the same ice-edge treatment to the fluke, just mirrored for its negative x-coordinate.

The bronze root plate also looks muddy and olive rather than metallic — I should brighten it toward a gilt or brass tone with less tarnish, and check why the plate renders asymmetrically on either side of the haft.

Checking the floating rocks and crystal clusters now, several sit at radii beyond the plinth edge (0.5-0.6 vs plinth 0.42), so I'll pull them inward to around 0.46-0.5 so they visually touch the plinth instead of hovering detached.

The front-left crystal cluster at 1.45 scale is too tall at 0.43 and hides the base, so I'll scale it down to 1.1. The haft's visible section between head and grip reads too thin at 0.034 radius, so I'm thickening it to 0.038 and giving it a lighter frost-blue tone for better contrast against the dark navy. The blade edge, top spear crystal, and fur ruff spikes all look fine as-is in the side view.

I want the blade to feel less flat, so I'll brighten its edge rim and lighten the body color near the root from dark navy to a lighter steel-blue gradient for better readability, and darken the fluke slightly. The bronze needs to be a brighter brass tone, and I'm finalizing the haft's color gradient along with closing in the rocks placement. Compiling edit list...

I'll replace both consecutive lines together in a single edit block.
